marble.name: Adding Fractions (Unlike Denominators)
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions to produce a common denominator
marble.prompt: If a recipe uses 2/3 of a cup of one ingredient and 3/4 of another, can you add those fractions together — even though the denominators are different?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Adds across the unlike denominators: 2/3 + 5/4 = 7/7, combining numerators and denominators.
Finds a common denominator but scales only one (or neither) numerator, or uses a wrong common denominator (2/3 = 2/12).

In mixed-number subtraction, subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger in each column regardless of position (does 12/20 − 5/20), never regrouping across the whole when the minuend's fraction part is smaller.
representations: Two strips/number lines re-gridded to a common denominator (thirds and quarters → twelfths)
Area/fraction-circle model showing both fractions recut to the shared unit
Mixed-number bars showing a whole tile broken into the common unit to enable borrowing (1 whole → 20/20)
Improper-fraction conversion as an alternative route (3 1/4 = 13/4) laid beside the mixed form

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Writes 7/7 (or similar) for the sum; denominators combined.
wrongAnswers.fix: Re-partition both fractions to a shared unit on strips; estimate first — 5/4 is already more than 1, so 2/3 + 5/4 must exceed 1, and 7/7 = 1 can't be right.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Correct common denominator but a numerator left unscaled (2/12 for 2/3); the equivalence is incomplete.
wrongAnswers.fix: Rebuild each equivalence on the model — thirds cut into twelfths turn ONE third into FOUR twelfths, so 2/3 = 8/12; the top scales by the same factor as the bottom. Check both conversions before combining.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Fraction part of the answer is 7/20 (took 5 from 12 the wrong way) or the child is stuck because '5/20 minus 12/20 can't be done'.
wrongAnswers.fix: Model regrouping a whole: break one whole of 3 1/4 into 20/20 so 3 5/20 becomes 2 25/20, then subtract; or convert both to improper fractions (65/20 − 32/20) to avoid the borrow. Reteach mixed↔improper conversion as the enabling move.
